concepts.title: Vegetative Propagation in Plants
concepts.definition: In brief, In brief, In brief, In brief, a mode of asexual reproduction where fresh plant organs grow from non-reproductive structures like roots, stems, or leaves without seed formation.
concepts.formula: concept method; no single closed formula
concepts.key_idea: Generates genetically identical plant clones directly from vegetative tissues.
question_patterns: how does vegetative propagation work in plants
explain cutting grafting and layering in horticulture
what are the benefits of vegetative reproduction in farming
describe tissue culture technique for plant multiplication

solution_steps.explain: Determine whether stems, roots, leaves, or apical meristem tips are utilized for propagation.
Explain techniques like stem cuttings, grafting stem slits, layering buried twigs, or tissue culture nutrient media.
State that offspring retain identical traits to the single parent without genetic recombination.

concepts.title: Asexual Reproduction by Budding and Spore Formation
concepts.definition: In brief, In brief, Asexual processes where new individuals originate either from cellular outgrowths called buds or from resilient unicellular spores produced in specialized sacs.
concepts.formula: concept method; no single closed formula
concepts.key_idea: In brief, Rapid asexual multiplication via mitosis that forms identical offspring clones.
question_patterns: how does hydra reproduce by budding
explain spore formation in fungi like rhizopus
describe asexual multiplication in yeast cells
how do spores spread and germinate in moist conditions

solution_steps.explain: Determine if the organism reproduces via bud detachment (Hydra/yeast) or airborne spore release (Rhizopus/Aspergillus).
Mitosis replicates identical genetic content into the budding outgrowth or spore nucleus.
Spores disperse lightly through air currents and germinate rapidly when moisture and warm temperatures are available.

concepts.title: Meiosis and Gamete Chromosome Reduction
concepts.definition: In brief, In brief, Specialized reductional cell division that reduces the diploid chromosome count of parent germ cells by half to generate haploid reproductive gametes.
concepts.key_idea: Halving chromosome numbers during gametogenesis maintains constant species chromosome counts across generations.
question_patterns: calculate haploid chromosome number from diploid count
how many chromosomes are in a human sperm or egg cell
find gamete chromosome count given somatic cell chromosome number
determine chromosome count in a fertilized zygote

solution_steps.explain: Divide total diploid cell chromosomes by two to get haploid gamete chromosome count.

concepts.title: Chromosomal Gamete Combinations and Genetic Variation
concepts.definition: The mathematical assortment of independent chromosome pairs during meiotic gamete formation, creating diverse genetic combinations.
concepts.key_idea: In brief, In brief, In brief, In brief, Random segregation of chromosome pairs exponentially increases gametic diversity.
question_patterns: calculate possible gamete combinations for given chromosome pairs
how many unique combinations are possible from n pairs of chromosomes
compute genetic variation potential from chromosome segregation
find total possible gamete assortments during meiosis

solution_steps.explain: Raise base 2 to the power of independent chromosome pair count.

concepts.title: Anatomy and Functions of Floral Organs
concepts.definition: The structural arrangement of angiosperm flowers into sepals, petals, stamens, and pistils dedicated to sexual reproduction.
concepts.formula: concept method; no single closed formula
concepts.key_idea: Stamens manufacture male pollen gametes while pistils house female egg ovules.
question_patterns: describe the four main whorls of a complete flower
what are the male and female reproductive organs of a flower
explain the structure of stamen and pistil
identify functions of sepals petals anther and stigma

solution_steps.explain: Sepals protect flower buds while bright fragrant petals attract animal pollinators.
Stamen consists of filament and anther producing pollen grains carrying male gametes.
Pistil consists of sticky stigma, tubelike style, and swollen ovary containing egg-bearing ovules.

concepts.title: Pollination Mechanics and Pollen-to-Seed Efficiency
concepts.definition: In brief, In brief, In brief, In brief, the move of pollen grains from anther to stigma via wind, water, or animal vectors, evaluated by the pollen grains needed per seed formed.
concepts.key_idea: Wind pollination requires massive excess pollen release compared to targeted animal pollination.
question_patterns: calculate pollen to seed ratio
determine pollen efficiency for wind vs insect pollination
compute average pollen grains expended per seed produced
find ratio of pollen grains released to seeds harvested

solution_steps.explain: Divide total pollen grains released by total seeds successfully formed.

concepts.title: Fertilisation and Reproductive Strategies in Animals
concepts.definition: In brief, In brief, the fusion of both both both both both both both both both both both both both both both both both both both both both both both both male and female gametes occurring either externally in aquatic environments or internally within the female body.
concepts.formula: concept method; no single closed formula
concepts.key_idea: External fertilisation relies on high egg quantities to offset loss, whereas internal fertilisation provides higher protection.
question_patterns: contrast external and internal fertilisation in animals
why do aquatic animals produce thousands of eggs
explain how zygote converts to embryo and fruit in plants
compare offspring survival rates between fish and birds

solution_steps.explain: Classify fertilization as external (outside body, in water) or internal (inside female organism).

solution_steps.action: analyze egg volume versus survival probability
solution_steps.explain: High egg loss from predators in water demands large clutch sizes, whereas internal development requires fewer eggs.
Zygote undergoes cell division into an embryo; in plants ovule forms seed and ovary forms fruit.

concepts.title: Human Reproductive Systems Anatomy
concepts.definition: The structural system of human male and female organs responsible for producing sperm and eggs, facilitating fertilization, and nourishing developing embryos.
concepts.formula: concept method; no single closed formula
concepts.key_idea: In brief, Testes in scrotum form sperm; ovaries produce both eggs and support uterine foetal development.
question_patterns: describe organs of male reproductive system and their functions
describe female reproductive organs and site of fertilisation
why are testes located inside the scrotum
what roles do accessory glands play in human male reproduction

solution_steps.explain: Testes in scrotum maintain lower temperature for sperm formation; vas deferens and glands transport sperm through urethra.
Ovaries release eggs; oviducts host fertilization; uterus provides muscular lining for embryo implantation.

concepts.title: Menstrual Cycle Timing and Ovulation Prediction
concepts.definition: The repeating monthly reproductive cycle in females involving uterine lining buildup, egg release during ovulation, and shedding via menstruation.
concepts.key_idea: Ovulation occurs roughly midpoint in the cycle while next menstruation follows one cycle length later.
question_patterns: calculate expected date of next menstrual period
predict next period date given cycle length and start day
determine approximate day of ovulation in menstrual cycle
find when menstruation cycle repeats

solution_steps.explain: Add full cycle length to the start date of the last menstrual period.

concepts.title: Contraception and Sexually Transmitted Infection Prevention
concepts.definition: Preventative medical and physical strategies used to avoid unplanned pregnancy and protect against sexually transmitted infections.
concepts.formula: concept method; no single closed formula
concepts.key_idea: Barrier methods prevent STI transmission and unintended pregnancy, while hormonal, IUD, and surgical methods prevent pregnancy.
question_patterns: what are different contraceptive methods available
how do condoms protect against STIs and pregnancy
explain operation of intrauterine devices like copper T
what are surgical methods of contraception in males and females

solution_steps.explain: Group into barrier devices (condoms), oral hormonal pills, IUDs (Copper-T), and surgical blockages (vasectomy/tubectomy).
Condoms act as mechanical barriers preventing direct fluid contact and stopping STI pathogens like HIV, syphilis, and gonorrhoea.

worked_examples.question_pattern: A human body cell contains {diploid_chromosomes} chromosomes. Calculate the number of chromosomes present in a human sperm cell.

solution_template.explain: Divide total diploid cell chromosomes by two to get haploid gamete chromosome count.

worked_examples.question_pattern: During meiotic simulation with {num_pairs} pairs of distinct chromosomes, calculate the total possible unique gamete combinations.

solution_template.explain: Raise base 2 to the power of independent chromosome pair count.

worked_examples.question_pattern: A wind-pollinated maize plant releases {total_pollen} pollen grains to produce {seeds_formed} seeds. Calculate the pollen to seed ratio.

solution_template.explain: Divide total pollen grains released by total seeds successfully formed.

worked_examples.question_pattern: Rina's menstrual cycle recurs every {cycle_length} days. Her last period began on day {last_period_day} of March. On which day of March is her next period expected to begin?

solution_template.explain: Add full cycle length to the start date of the last menstrual period.
